root_cause: The frame-size detection logic added in commit 93b0ca26ac ("better frame size detection for old codecs") assumes that for old ANIMv0/1 (subversion < 2) files the internal frame is always exactly 384x242, and unconditionally trusts this fixed size without cross-checking it against the actually parsed FOBJ w/h fields, which are only bounded by a much looser generic check (w<=800, h<=600). This allows fields not fitting the assumed fixed buffer to pass through.
findings: In process_frame_obj(), when ctx->subversion < 2 (Rebel Assault 1 ANIMv0/1 files), the internal frame buffer dimensions are hard-coded to xres=384, yres=242, and ctx->have_dimensions is set to 1 without validating that the FOBJ's own w/h (and implicitly left/top placement) fit within this 384x242 buffer.
